function: Unsupervised DNNs map large-scale fading coefficients to the square-root downlink power coefficients of each RU-UE pair, scaling fixed MR or RZF precoders under per-RU power limits (p. 6).
system: Cell-free massive MIMO downlink: L=16 RUs with N=4 antennas, K=20 single-antenna UEs, 1000 m x 1000 m, 2 GHz carrier, 20 MHz bandwidth, no RIS (p. 10).
method: Unsupervised learning with custom loss functions (sum-SE, max-min SINR, max-prod SINR); fully connected DNN at the CPU or one per RU, with optional side information (pp. 5-9).
data_channel: Own simulator: correlated Rayleigh fading with path loss from refs [2], [4]; 50,000 realizations split 90/10 into training and validation; 10,000 independent test UE distributions (p. 10).
test_conditions: Training on a fixed 16-RU topology with random UE drops; testing on 10,000 independent drops, orthogonal and non-orthogonal pilots, and a 1 dB log-normal shadowing perturbation (pp. 10, 13).
baselines: Non-learned: equal power, heuristic scheme [26], WMMSE-ADMM optimization [4]. Learned: supervised DNN of [16] (pp. 11, 13).
metrics: CDF of spectral efficiency per UE, total spectral efficiency, total energy efficiency, minimum SINR CDF, Jain's fairness index, inference time (pp. 9-13).
complexity: Tables 1-3 give parameters per layer; Table 4 gives inference time 0.55-5.2 ms versus ADMM 88.6-131.7 ms; big-O for the DNN and O(L^3 K) for ADMM (pp. 8-9).
q1_support: p. 3: "is modeled by correlated Rayleigh fading". Not met: custom Rayleigh simulator; its path loss (Eq. 22, p. 10) comes from refs [2], [4], with no standardized channel model or measured data.
q2_support: p. 13: "we evaluate the trained centralized and distributed DNNs with a perturbated version of the dataset"
q3_support: p. 13: "significantly outperform the heuristic power allocation solution [26] by more than 20%"; p. 13: "even the supervised counterpart from [16] is outperformed by our distributed and centralized DNN models"
q4_support: p. 9: "the inference time provided by the DNN models is shown in Tab. 4"
q5_support: p. 10: "50, 000 network realizations are considered, each generated with different UE locations given a fixed RUs deployment topology". Not met: simulated data, no code or data link, no public channel dataset.
notes: Area 3 is borderline on function: the DNN outputs only the power coefficients that scale fixed MR/RZF precoding vectors (p. 4 Eq. 10, p. 6), counted here as the power part of the BS precoder; if the protocol treats power-only control as outside area 3, exclude with code function. The RU selection (Eq. 21, p. 9) is a non-learned criterion. q2 rests on one shadowing perturbation (1 dB, truncated at 3 dB, p. 13) that the reviewer may judge a CSI-error-type test; the number of UEs is handled with separate pre-trained weights (p. 7). Text cites the heuristic scheme as [26], Fig. 10 as [24].
